inputs.question: Why is CI failing on PR 42?

outputs.reference: The webhook secret check runs after the run is created, so a bad secret returns 200 instead of 401. Fix: check the secret before creating the run.

offline_trajectory.answer: PR 42 fails tests/test_surfaces.py::test_webhook_rejects_bad_secret: the test expects 401 for a bad secret but gets 200. The PR moved the secret check after the run is created, so an unauthenticated request still triggers an agent run. Fix: verify the secret before creating the run and return 401 early, as in src/agent_factory/surfaces/webhook.py. Do not change the test.

inputs.question: Explain how the tool allowlist middleware works

outputs.reference: ToolAllowlistMiddleware in src/agent_factory/middleware.py overrides wrap_tool_call and returns an error ToolMessage for tools not in the allowed set.

offline_trajectory.answer: ToolAllowlistMiddleware lives in src/agent_factory/middleware.py. It overrides wrap_tool_call: if the requested tool name is not in the agent's allowed set (approved registry tools plus Deep Agents built-ins), it returns a ToolMessage with status=error prefixed BLOCKED_BY_POLICY instead of calling the handler. The model only ever sees approved tools at build time, so this is defense in depth against hallucinated or injected tool names.
